nodes.label: ensure_installed Lists Invariant
nodes.rationale: lsp-config.lua (mason-lspconfig) and treesitter.lua keep independent ensure_installed lists; adding a language usually requires editing both.

nodes.label: install.sh Gotchas
nodes.rationale: Skips installing nodejs/npm via apt when node >=18 is already on PATH because apt's npm conflicts with NodeSource installs; uses numeric (not string) Neovim version comparison since string compare gets 0.11 < 0.9 wrong; backs up pre-existing ~/.config/nvim and ~/.tmux.conf with a timestamp suffix before symlinking.

nodes.label: lazy.nvim Auto-Discovery Plugin Architecture
nodes.rationale: nvim/lua/plugins.lua intentionally returns {} because the plugins/ directory shadows it when lazy.setup("plugins") runs; adding a plugin means adding a new file under nvim/lua/plugins/, not registering specs elsewhere.

nodes.label: Repo Purpose: Nvim+Tmux Dotfiles
nodes.rationale: install.sh symlinks nvim/ and tmux/tmux.conf directly into $HOME, so editing repo files directly modifies the user's live editor config; there is no build step because the repo IS the deployed config.

nodes.label: Tmux <-> Nvim Pane Navigation Invariant
nodes.rationale: Both Ctrl-h/j/k/l and Alt-h/j/k/l are bound because some terminals send Ctrl-h as Backspace; C-j is intentionally nvim-only so shells can use it to submit multiline input outside nvim (use M-j there instead). Changing one side requires changing the other.

nodes.label: Treesitter Python Master-Branch Pin
nodes.rationale: Python parser is pinned to the master branch revision and shipped with custom highlights.scm/indents.scm because nvim-treesitter's upstream indent query doesn't compile against the master parser, which would otherwise make every new Python line indent to column 0.

nodes.label: Catppuccin Highlight Overrides Invariant
nodes.rationale: Highlights are applied twice (custom_highlights, then a ColorScheme autocmd) because some plugins re-apply their own highlights after setup() and would clobber the first pass; the autocmd is load-bearing and must not be removed.

nodes.label: Atomic Cutover (Task 5)
nodes.rationale: The three edits (slim catppuccin spec, wire orchestrator in init.lua, which-key entries) must land in one commit because any subset would leave the editor in a broken state, e.g. a slimmed catppuccin spec with no orchestrator wired means no theme applied at all.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Architecture (plugin specs vs theme modules)
nodes.norm_label: two-layer architecture (plugin specs vs theme modules)
nodes.rationale: lazy.nvim's config field only fires once per session, but the transparency toggle needs to re-run setup at runtime with a new value; splitting plain Lua theme modules out of the plugin specs lets startup and runtime toggle share the same M.setup({transparent}) code path with no duplicated configuration.

nodes.label: Out-of-Scope Decisions (Indent Guides)
nodes.rationale: Filetype exclusions skipped since ibl's defaults already skip help/lazy/dashboard buffers; buffer-local toggle rejected in favor of the simpler global on/off mental model; persistence across restarts rejected as premature; scope-only sub-toggle and custom indent character deferred as unnecessary now.

nodes.label: Per-Theme Adapter Contract (M.setup({transparent}))
nodes.rationale: Absorbs each plugin's per-vendor option name (transparent_background, transparent, disable_background) so the orchestrator only ever knows about a single boolean.

nodes.label: Catppuccin Refactor Rationale
nodes.rationale: Without a pattern gate, catppuccin's ColorScheme autocmd would clobber other themes by re-applying mocha overrides after switching to kanagawa; fixed with pattern="catppuccin*". Setup logic also can't be re-run because it lives inside lazy.nvim's config function, which only fires once, so it moves into themes/catppuccin.lua exposing M.setup(opts).

nodes.label: Out-of-Scope Decisions (Theme Switcher)
nodes.rationale: Catppuccin flavour switcher, per-theme custom highlights for kanagawa/vscode/rose-pine, a picker-style switcher (explicitly rejected during brainstorming in favor of dedicated keymaps), lazy-loading inactive themes (adds startup-vs-toggle code paths for ~50ms saved), and a random/cycle keymap were all left out of scope.

nodes.label: Plugin Choice: indent-blankline.nvim over mini.indentscope/hlchunk.nvim
nodes.rationale: ibl shows guides at every level (the standard look) rather than only the current scope like mini.indentscope; ibl is the de-facto standard with a built-in :IBLToggle command and a maintained catppuccin integration, unlike hlchunk.nvim.

nodes.label: ibl Plugin Spec Details (main=ibl, event, opts, keys)
nodes.norm_label: ibl plugin spec details (main=ibl, event, opts, keys)
nodes.rationale: main="ibl" is required since ibl's setup module is require("ibl"), not the repo name; loading via BufReadPost/BufNewFile instead of keys avoids a first-press-does-nothing bug where the key press would load the plugin (auto-enabling guides) and then immediately toggle them off.

nodes.label: Move find_files Binding from <C-p> to <leader>ff
nodes.rationale: Surfaces the binding in the which-key popup next to sibling find-actions (<leader>fg live grep, <leader><leader> oldfiles) and frees up <C-p> for future use; verified via grep that no other <C-p> references exist in the repo.
